newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans evacuate after floods, more on standby.
newsitem.headline: Germans evacuate after floods, more on standby.

text.p: Soldiers started evacuating thousands of people from their homes on Friday after a second dike burst overnight in the flood-hit Oder river area of eastern Germany.
Officials said about 3,000 people in the villages of Ziltendorf and Wiesenau would have to leave as a result of the breach, south of another dike which burst on Wednesday.

Further north in the Oderbruch area, local televsion broadcast messages warning the residents in around 15 villages to be prepared for evacuations after the foundations of a dike were swept away by the strong river currents.
Fire sirens and church bells sounded in the area to warn residents of the new danger.
A spokesman for the regional authorities said evacuations were progressing slowly as some residents were reluctant to follow orders and leave their homes.
The new breach was now 75 metres wide and would probably open up to 200 metres as water rushed through, he said.
Water levels slipped further downstream at Frankfurt an der Oder, which forms part of the border to Poland, after the breach relieved pressure.
But the situation in Ratzdorf, where the Oder and Neisse converge, was still critical, the spokesman said.

Germany so far has escaped the worst of the regional flooding -- the most serious in centuries -- which claimed more than 100 lives and inundated thousands of homes earlier this month in the neighbouring Czech Republic and Poland.

But German towns have been hit by power cuts and overflowing sewers. About 500 people were ordered to leave parts of the danger zone earlier this week, and farmers have started moving out thousands of head of livestock.
